subject: Urgent: surge in latency & 5xx after ModelPack 4.0q rollout (Harborside)
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <ops@harborside-retail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace Lin <grace.lin@harborside-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production impact after ModelPack 4.0q deploy — p95 latency + 5xx surge

Irene,

We pushed your ModelPack 4.0q (tag v4.0q-20261122) to our production traffic at ~08:45 PST and immediately started seeing p95 latency jump from ~220ms to ~1.4s and 5xx rate rise to ~2.7% (was ~0.04%). This is affecting our checkout flows; page errors reported by customers.

Attached a short CSV of p50/p95/p99 over the last 2 hours and a small set of traces. Can you confirm whether this rollout had any change to the quantization profile or runtime kernels? We need an ETA for mitigation — our CTO is on a call at 10:30.

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
SRE Lead, Harborside Retail
Attachments: harborside_perf_summary_1123.csv, request_traces_1123.txt

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <ops@harborside-retail.com>
Cc: Grace Lin <grace.lin@harborside-retail.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact after ModelPack 4.0q deploy — p95 latency + 5xx surge

Alex —

Thanks for the quick report and the traces. I'm escalating internally now and will coordinate a mitigation plan. Initial read: v4.0q included a new qprofile (qv2-small-int4) plus a kernel change for attention caching which can affect tail latency in heavy short-sequence workloads.

Immediate plan: 1) roll requests for Harborside back to v3.9 (hotfix channel) while we triage; 2) collect full traces and kv cache hit ratios; 3) if rollback not possible from your side, we can route your traffic to a compatible variant in our hosted pool.

I'm adding Rishi (serving/runtime) and Ben (customer success) to the thread. Will update within 20 minutes.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Alex Mercer <ops@harborside-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact after ModelPack 4.0q deploy — p95 latency + 5xx surge

Alex / Irene —

We dug into the quick traces. Observations:
- A subset of short-sequence requests (avg tokens < 24) show increased decode stall time after qv2-small-int4 is applied due to a fallback path that triggers slower fp16 kernels for certain activation ranges.
- 5xxs correlate with OOM/retry behavior on nodes with mixed quant kernels under high concurrency.

Immediate mitigation options:
- Rollback to v3.9 (recommended) — fastest recovery.
- If rollback not possible from Harborside's deploy system, we can (a) pin routing to v3.9 on Redwood side for your API key, or (b) force a compatible qprofile (qv1-int8) for your traffic.

Ben/Grace, can you confirm routing pin availability and whether we can force qprofile for a specific key?

Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Attachments: diag_qprofile_snapshot.json

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Alex Mercer <ops@harborside-retail.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact after ModelPack 4.0q deploy — p95 latency + 5xx surge

Alex — quick update from ops: we can immediately pin Harborside's API key to v3.9 from our control plane and apply a temporary qprofile override. I will schedule the pin now and confirm when traffic is on the fallback path. Expect 7–10 minutes.

Action items for Harborside: if you can halt any further local re-deploys for the next 20 minutes that will avoid flip-flop. We will monitor p95 and 5xx as soon as the pin completes.

Ben Carter
Customer Success — Escalations, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Mercer <ops@harborside-retail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact after ModelPack 4.0q deploy — p95 latency + 5xx surge

Ben/Irene —

Thank you — pin in progress on our side; we’ve frozen the deploy window. Confirming our side will accept traffic routed to v3.9. Please let us know when you see p95 fall back. Our CTO asked that we copy him if we need an extended mitigation.

Alex

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production impact after ModelPack 4.0q deploy — p95 latency + 5xx surge

Alex — follow-up and summary for executives: 

Timeline & impact:
- 08:45 PST: Harborside rolled v4.0q (included qv2-small-int4).
- 08:50–09:05 PST: p95 increased to ~1.4s, 5xx rose to ~2.7% affecting checkout traffic.
- 09:12 PST: Harborside alerted Redwood.
- 09:40 PST: Redwood pinned Harborside API key to v3.9 and applied qprofile override; progressive routing completed by 09:50 PST.
- 10:00 PST: p95 returned to baseline (~240ms), 5xx < 0.1%.

Root cause (preliminary): a new int4 qprofile introduced a regression path that for some short-input activation ranges falls back to a slower fp16/slow-atten kernel while also increasing memory pressure on mixed-quant nodes. Under Harborside's traffic burst pattern this produced decode stalls and occasional OOMs leading to retries (5xx).

Mitigations taken:
- Immediate routing pin to v3.9 and qv1-int8 override for Harborside — recovered service.
- We are opening a dedicated incident ticket (INF-8721) to: capture full traces, reproduce in staging, and add guardrails to prevent qv2-small-int4 from being selected for short-sequence-heavy keys by default.
- Engineering will block auto-rollout of qv2-small-int4 to customers who have not opted into experimental kernels until we resolve the fallback path.

Next steps & ETA:
- Engineering (Rishi) to deliver a root-cause write-up and a failing test case by EOD tomorrow.
- Product/CS (Ben) to coordinate with Harborside on a postmortem and a policy for targeted rollouts.
- Exec summary for Harborside leadership by 14:00 PST today (copying Markus and CS leadership).

Apologies for the disruption — we know this caused customer-facing failures. We will share the full incident notes and the timeline. Alex, please let us know if you need an executive call; we can make time today.

—Irene Choi
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
